findings.title: Silence menu item does nothing in the new list view
findings.body: In the list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` (GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47), so `rule` is undefined. `canSilence` now comes out true from the promRule path (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:96), so the 'Silence notifications' item shows up (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:126-131). Its handler sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and here it is false. Clicking the item does nothing and shows no error. The new test at GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:194 only checks that the item is present, so it never catches this. Fix: also render the drawer for a Grafana alerting `promRule`, using a variant of `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` that accepts the prom rule's uid and labels, or hide the item when no drawer can be shown.

findings.title: Pause and Delete are gone from the list view menu even when the prom-rule abilities allow them
findings.body: This PR computes `grafanaPauseAbility` and `grafanaDeleteAbility` from `promRule` and ORs them into `canPause` and `canDelete` (lines 83, 87). The menu still requires a ruler rule for both items: `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). The list view no longer passes a ruler rule (GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47), so the promRule-derived Pause and Delete abilities never matter. Before this PR, list items got `rule={rulerRule}` (old GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx), so users could pause and delete from the list. That ability is now quietly removed. The new test at GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:205-207 asserts exactly 4 menu items, which locks in the missing Delete. Fix: allow both items when a Grafana `promRule` is present. Delete only needs `identifier` and `groupIdentifier` (DeleteModal.tsx:35). Pause needs `MenuItemPauseRule` to work from a uid or prom rule.

findings.title: `key` prop dropped from GrafanaRuleListItem inside `rules.map`
findings.body: The old `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} …/>` had a key. The replacement does not, even though `key` is still destructured at line 152 and the other branches still pass it (lines 165, 169). React will warn about missing keys. It will also reconcile list items by index, so when the filter results change or more results load, per-item state such as an open delete modal, the silence drawer or the clone redirect can stay attached to the wrong rule. Add `key={key}`.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleListItem` built `href` with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, where `returnTo = createReturnTo()`. The new component drops `returnTo`. After opening a rule from a filtered or searched list, the rule page's back/return navigation no longer returns to the list state the user came from. Keep `{ returnTo: createReturnTo() }`, unless this was intentionally removed, in which case the PR should say so.

findings.title: Test treats losing Delete/Pause as expected behaviour
findings.body: The test grants AlertingRuleDelete and AlertingRuleUpdate in `beforeEach` (lines 48-62), then asserts the menu has exactly 4 items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). With delete permission granted, a correct menu would include Delete. Pause probably as well, since the fixture rule appears to be an unprovisioned alerting rule (not verified). The assertion records the regression described on AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 rather than catching it. It also never clicks Silence to check that a drawer opens.

findings.title: Every list row now runs both the ruler and prom ability hooks, twice
findings.body: `RuleActionsButtons.V2` and `AlertRuleMenu` each call the ruler hook (`useRulerRuleAbility`/`useRulerRuleAbilities`) and the prom hook (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`). In the list view the ruler rule is always undefined, so per row that is 2× `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (including `useIsRuleEditable` and `useCanSilence`) doing no useful work, plus 2× `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, each with its own `useFolder` and `useFolderPermissions`. RTK Query dedups the network requests, but the hook work and memo churn repeat for every rule on a page this PR is meant to make lighter. Consider computing abilities once in `RuleActionsButtons` and passing them down, or skipping the ruler path when `rule` is undefined.

contracts.action: Silence menu item in the new list view (promRule only)
contracts.equivalent_path: Old list item passed rulerRule, so SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rendered on click
contracts.before_after: handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer; the drawer renders only when `rule` is a ruler alerting rule
contracts.visible_effect: The menu item shows but clicking it opens nothing

contracts.action: Pause/Delete menu items gated on promRule abilities
contracts.equivalent_path: Ruler-based abilities with a rulerRule present
contracts.before_after: canPause/canDelete OR in the prom abilities, but rendering still requires rulerRule
contracts.visible_effect: Pause and Delete never appear in the list view

contracts.before_after: Fetches the folder via useFolder; reports not editable while loading or when the folder is missing
contracts.visible_effect: The Edit button is hidden until the folder loads
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder request fails, folder is undefined and the rule is shown as non-editable with no error
contracts.open_question: Does useFolder surface errors, or does a failed request only hide the Edit button with no message?

summary: The change moves the new rule list to Grafana prom rules only, but the action menu still assumes a ruler rule is present. As a result, Silence shows up but does nothing when clicked, and Pause and Delete disappear even when the user has the permissions. FilterView also lost the `key` on Grafana list items, and the rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts the reduced 4-item menu, which locks in the missing Delete.
